reference: util-linux flock is the independent CLI oracle for private regular-file locks, bounded conflicts, child status and file effects. Bash type/help and documented version text are separate metadata contracts.
coverage: Bash reports flock as a builtin with type -t.
Bash help contains the documented FD and file command forms and principal options.
Bash short help exposes the registered synopsis.
The loadable's documented version metadata is stable.
Private-file FD lifetime/unlock, shared and exclusive conflicts, bounded waits, file command effects/status, close/no-fork modes and parser/open errors.
exclusions: Release-before-deadline synchronization and inherited-descriptor observations require an additional bounded process fixture; no stress timing or host lock files are used.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash registers flock as a builtin using the Bash type -t contract.
Check the full Bash help text against the pinned documented forms, option spellings, and conflict behavior without invoking a lock operation.
cases.script:
h=$(help flock) || exit 1
[[ $h == *"Manage advisory file locks via flock(2)."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FD"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE command [args...]"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *'flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE -c "shell command"'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--shared"* && $h == *"--exclusive"* && $h == *"--unlock"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--nonblock"* && $h == *"--wait"* && $h == *"--conflict-exit-code"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--close"* && $h == *"--no-fork"* && $h == *"--command"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check Bash help -s output against the synopsis registered in flock_struct.short_doc and Bash help builtin formatting.
cases.stdout: flock: flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] [-E N] FD | FILE [command [args] | -c CMD]

cases.purpose: Check the loadable's documented version response; --version exits before opening an operand or acquiring a lock.
Compare FD lock lifetime, independent-open conflict and explicit unlock using a private file.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -xn 8
if flock -xn 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'held=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9
printf 'released
'

cases.purpose: Compare compatible shared locks and configured exclusive conflict status on separate private open descriptions.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -sn 8
flock -sn 9
if flock -xn -E 23 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'exclusive=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9

cases.purpose: A small bounded timed conflict returns the configured status, then acquisition succeeds after release.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -xn 8
if flock -x -w 0.02 -E 24 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'timeout=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -x -w 0.02 9
flock -u 9

cases.purpose: Compare private lock-file creation, shell command effects, exit status and release after child completion.
cases.script:
if flock lock -c 'printf "payload\n" > result; exit 7'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'child=%s\n' "$rc"
flock -n lock -c 'printf "released\n"'

cases.purpose: Compare close/no-fork command modes and incompatible options on private files; no-fork runs in a disposable subshell.
cases.script:
flock -o lock -c 'printf close > closed'
if (flock -F lock -c 'printf nofork > direct; exit 9'); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'nofork=%s\n' "$rc"
if flock -Fo lock -c 'printf forbidden > unexpected'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'incompatible=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ ! -e unexpected ]]

cases.purpose: Compare malformed-option and missing-parent open errors, retaining diagnostics and creation effects.
cases.script:
for arg in bad ''; do
 if flock -w "$arg" lock; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf 'timeout=%s\n' "$rc"
done
if flock -E 256 lock; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'exit-code=%s\n' "$rc"
if flock missing/lock -c 'printf unexpected'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'open=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare the actual negative-timeout error status on an uncontended private descriptor, including reference timer setup errors, without assuming parser behavior.
cases.script:
exec 9>lock
if flock -w -1 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf "negative-wait=%s\n" "$rc"

cases.purpose: Reject missing operands with explicit util-linux usage status.
A closed private descriptor reports data-error65.
A nonnegative descriptor outside the int range is a usage failure before any lock attempt.
A lone nonnumeric operand is an invalid descriptor and must not create a file.
Reject extra arguments after FILE -c CMD before file creation or child execution.
Reject extra operands with prefix -c without creating or executing anything.
With a command, an all-digit operand names a private file rather than a descriptor.
Finite negative wait reports timer-error71 even when -n is also specified.
A missing-parent open error66 precedes negative-wait timer setup.
Negative-wait timer setup precedes closed-descriptor locking, without installing any timer in the embedding shell.
A valid file form opens its private file before negative-wait timer failure and never runs the child.
After caught negative-wait and incompatible-mode errors, preserve descriptor ownership, leave no lock/child effects, and execute a later valid file command in the same shell.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
if flock -w -1 -E 23 8; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 71 ]]
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9
if flock -Fo untouched -c 'printf forbidden > marker'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 64 && ! -e untouched && ! -e marker ]]
flock -n -w 0 lock -c 'printf recovered > result'
printf 'recovered\n'
